title.value: A stochastic integer programming approach to reserve staff scheduling with preferences
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: A stochastic integer programming approach to reserve staff scheduling with preferences

extractions.description: The paper addresses the reserve staff scheduling problem in the transit industry, considering employee satisfaction and uncertainty in demand. It formulates a two-stage stochastic integer program to optimize days-off scheduling for reserve employees, incorporating their preferences and minimizing service cancellations.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses optimization within the transit industry, it doesn't explicitly focus on broader Sustainable Development Goals. The primary focus is on efficient resource allocation and employee satisfaction within a specific operational context.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We tackle a new variant of the personnel scheduling problem under unknown demand by considering employee satisfaction via endogenous uncertainty depending on the combination of their preferred and received schedules.

primary_category.justification: The paper's primary focus is on optimization within the transit industry. It doesn't directly address climate change, natural systems, pollution, or other environmental concerns. Therefore, it doesn't align with any of the predefined primary categories.
primary_category.quote: We address this problem in the context of reserve staff scheduling, an unstudied operational problem from the transit industry.

primary_sub_category.quote: To handle the challenges brought by the two uncertainty sources, regular employee and reserve employee absences, we formulate this problem as a two-stage stochastic integer program with mixed-integer recourse.
